BTC: Bitcoin is the first decentralized cryptocurrency, launched in 2009 by the pseudonymous Satoshi Nakamoto. It runs on a proof-of-work blockchain with a fixed maximum supply of 21 million coins.
ETH: Ethereum is a programmable proof-of-stake blockchain whose native asset, ether, pays for transactions and smart-contract execution. Most DeFi, stablecoin and NFT activity, as well as many layer-2 networks, settle on Ethereum.
USDT: Tether (USDT) is the largest stablecoin by market capitalization, designed to track the US dollar 1:1 and backed by reserves held by Tether. It is issued on many blockchains, including Tron and Ethereum.
XRP: XRP is the native asset of the XRP Ledger, an open-source blockchain built for fast, low-cost payments and asset transfers. Ripple uses XRP in some of its cross-border payment products.
SOL: Solana is a high-throughput layer-1 blockchain that combines proof-of-stake with Proof of History for fast block times. SOL pays transaction fees and secures the network through staking.
BNB: BNB is the native coin of BNB Chain and the utility token of the Binance ecosystem. It pays gas fees on BNB Smart Chain and is used for trading-fee discounts on Binance.
USDC: USD Coin (USDC) is a fully reserved US-dollar stablecoin issued by Circle, redeemable 1:1 for dollars. It is widely used for trading, payments and DeFi across many blockchains.
DOGE: Dogecoin started in 2013 as a light-hearted fork of Litecoin's codebase and became one of the most widely held cryptocurrencies. It uses proof-of-work and has no maximum supply.
ADA: Cardano is a proof-of-stake layer-1 blockchain developed with a research-driven, peer-reviewed approach. ADA is used for fees, staking and on-chain governance.
TRX: TRON is a layer-1 blockchain known for low-fee transfers and is one of the largest networks for USDT stablecoin payments. TRX pays for network resources and is used for staking and governance.
AVAX: Avalanche is a smart-contract platform built around fast-finality consensus and customizable layer-1 networks. AVAX pays fees on the C-Chain and secures the network through staking.
GRAM: Gram is the native coin of The Open Network (TON), a blockchain closely integrated with Telegram. It was called Toncoin (TON) until a June 2026 community vote renamed it Gram; balances and addresses did not change.
LINK: Chainlink is a decentralized oracle network that delivers off-chain data such as price feeds to smart contracts, plus cross-chain messaging (CCIP). LINK pays node operators and is used for staking.
SHIB: Shiba Inu is a dog-themed memecoin launched on Ethereum in 2020. Its ecosystem includes the ShibaSwap exchange and the Shibarium layer-2 network.
SUI: Sui is a layer-1 blockchain that uses the Move programming language and an object-centric data model to process many transactions in parallel. SUI pays gas and is used for staking.
DOT: Polkadot is a multi-chain network in which specialized blockchains share security and communicate with each other. DOT is used for governance, staking and buying blockspace.
BCH: Bitcoin Cash is a 2017 fork of Bitcoin that increased the block size to allow more transactions per block and lower fees. It uses proof-of-work and the same 21 million coin cap.
NEAR: NEAR Protocol is a sharded proof-of-stake layer-1 focused on usability, chain abstraction and AI-related applications. NEAR pays for transactions and storage and secures the network.
LTC: Litecoin is one of the oldest cryptocurrencies, created in 2011 as a faster, lighter alternative to Bitcoin. It uses proof-of-work (Scrypt) with a maximum supply of 84 million coins.
UNI: UNI is the governance token of Uniswap, one of the largest decentralized exchanges, which uses automated market makers to swap tokens on Ethereum and many other networks.
PEPE: Pepe is a frog-themed memecoin launched on Ethereum in 2023. It has no utility beyond trading and community and is among the largest memecoins by market capitalization.
APT: Aptos is a layer-1 blockchain built with the Move language by former Diem engineers, designed for parallel transaction execution. APT pays gas and secures the network through staking.
ICP: The Internet Computer, developed by the DFINITY Foundation, is a blockchain that can host full applications, websites and data on-chain. ICP is converted into 'cycles' to pay for computation and is used in governance.
DAI: Dai is a decentralized, crypto-collateralized stablecoin soft-pegged to the US dollar, originally issued by MakerDAO and now part of the Sky ecosystem alongside USDS.
TAO: Bittensor is a decentralized network for machine learning in which specialized subnets reward participants with TAO for producing useful AI outputs. TAO has a 21 million maximum supply.
ETC: Ethereum Classic is the original Ethereum chain that continued unchanged after the 2016 DAO fork. It remains a proof-of-work smart-contract platform.
XMR: Monero is a privacy-focused cryptocurrency that hides senders, receivers and amounts by default using ring signatures, stealth addresses and RingCT. It is mined with the CPU-friendly RandomX algorithm.
RENDER: Render Network is a decentralized GPU marketplace that connects people who need 3D rendering and AI compute with node operators who have spare GPU capacity. RENDER pays for that work.
POL: POL is the native token of Polygon, which replaced MATIC 1:1 in 2024. It secures Polygon PoS and is used across Polygon's payments and AggLayer infrastructure.
KAS: Kaspa is a proof-of-work cryptocurrency built on a blockDAG (GHOSTDAG) that allows many blocks to be produced in parallel, giving fast block times while staying decentralized.
FET: Artificial Superintelligence Alliance (FET) was formed by merging the Fetch.ai and SingularityNET token ecosystems to support decentralized AI agents and infrastructure.
XLM: Stellar is an open payments network for issuing assets and moving money across borders quickly and cheaply. XLM pays network fees and serves as a bridge asset.
HBAR: Hedera is a public ledger that uses hashgraph consensus and is governed by a council of large organizations. HBAR pays network fees and secures the network through staking.
OKB: OKB is the utility token of the OKX exchange, used for trading-fee discounts and as the gas token of OKX's X Layer network.
STX: Stacks is a Bitcoin layer that brings smart contracts and DeFi to Bitcoin, including the sBTC bridge. STX is used for fees and in Stacks' Proof of Transfer consensus.
FIL: Filecoin is a decentralized storage network where providers earn FIL for storing data and proving they still hold it.
ARB: Arbitrum is a leading Ethereum layer-2 that uses optimistic rollups to make transactions faster and cheaper. ARB is the governance token of the Arbitrum DAO.
AAVE: Aave is one of the largest decentralized lending protocols, letting users supply and borrow crypto assets across many chains. AAVE is used for governance and protocol safety staking.
IMX: Immutable is a gaming-focused ecosystem that includes Immutable zkEVM. IMX pays fees and is used for staking and governance.
OP: Optimism is an Ethereum layer-2 rollup and the foundation of the OP Stack 'Superchain' used by many other networks. OP is the governance token of the Optimism Collective.
INJ: Injective is a layer-1 blockchain built for finance applications such as on-chain order books, derivatives and tokenized assets. INJ is used for staking, governance and fee burns.
WIF: dogwifhat is a Solana memecoin based on an image of a dog wearing a knitted hat. It is purely community-driven, with no utility beyond trading.
ATOM: Cosmos Hub is the original chain of the Cosmos ecosystem of interoperable blockchains connected through IBC. ATOM secures the Hub and is used for governance.
MNT: Mantle is an Ethereum layer-2 network. MNT pays gas on Mantle and is used for governance of the Mantle ecosystem.
VET: VeChain is a layer-1 blockchain focused on supply-chain tracking, sustainability and enterprise data. VET generates VTHO, which pays transaction fees.
BONK: Bonk is a dog-themed memecoin on Solana, launched in late 2022 with a large community airdrop, and integrated into many Solana apps.
GRT: The Graph is a decentralized protocol for indexing and querying blockchain data. GRT is staked by indexers and used to pay for queries.
RUNE: THORChain is a cross-chain liquidity network that lets users swap native assets such as BTC and ETH without wrapping them. RUNE is paired in every pool and bonded by node operators.
SEI: Sei is a layer-1 blockchain optimized for trading, with fast finality and a parallelized EVM. SEI pays gas and secures the network through staking.
THETA: Theta Network is a decentralized video delivery and edge-computing network. THETA is used for staking and governance; the companion TFUEL token pays for operations.
AR: Arweave is a decentralized storage network designed for permanent data storage paid with a single up-front fee in AR.
ONDO: Ondo Finance tokenizes real-world assets such as US Treasuries and equities for use on blockchains. ONDO is the governance token of the Ondo ecosystem.
ALGO: Algorand is a pure proof-of-stake layer-1 blockchain with fast finality, designed by MIT professor Silvio Micali. ALGO pays fees and is used for staking and governance.
SKY: Sky is the rebranded MakerDAO ecosystem, issuer of the USDS and DAI stablecoins. MKR holders can upgrade to SKY at a rate of 1 MKR = 24,000 SKY, which is used for governance and rewards.
FLOKI: FLOKI is a memecoin named after Elon Musk's dog that has expanded into gaming (Valhalla), education and DeFi products.
TIA: Celestia is a modular blockchain that specializes in data availability, letting rollups publish their data cheaply. TIA pays for blobspace and secures the network.
JUP: Jupiter is the leading swap aggregator on Solana, also offering perpetuals and limit orders. JUP is used for governance of the Jupiter DAO.
PYTH: Pyth Network is an oracle that publishes high-frequency market data from exchanges and trading firms to many blockchains. PYTH is used for governance and staking.
HNT: Helium is a decentralized wireless network for IoT and 5G/mobile coverage, run on Solana. Hotspot operators earn HNT for providing coverage.
LDO: Lido is the largest liquid-staking protocol, issuing stETH to people who stake ETH through it. LDO is the governance token of the Lido DAO.
FDUSD: First Digital USD (FDUSD) is a US-dollar stablecoin issued by First Digital and backed by cash and cash-equivalent reserves.
VIRTUAL: Virtuals Protocol is a platform for creating, tokenizing and co-owning AI agents, mainly on Base. VIRTUAL is paired with each agent token and used throughout the ecosystem.
ENA: Ethena is the protocol behind USDe, a synthetic dollar backed by crypto collateral and hedged with derivatives positions. ENA is its governance token.
JASMY: JasmyCoin powers a Japanese IoT and data-sharing platform that lets users control and monetize data generated by their devices.
POPCAT: Popcat is a Solana memecoin based on the 'Popcat' internet meme. It is community-driven, with no utility beyond trading.
PENDLE: Pendle is a DeFi protocol that splits yield-bearing assets into principal and yield tokens so users can trade future yield. PENDLE is used for governance and fee sharing.
STRK: Starknet is an Ethereum layer-2 validity rollup that uses STARK proofs and the Cairo language. STRK is used for fees, staking and governance.
GALA: Gala is the token of Gala Games, a blockchain gaming platform that also runs its own GalaChain. GALA is used for in-game purchases and node rewards.
RAY: Raydium is an automated market maker and liquidity provider on Solana. RAY is used for liquidity mining and staking.
AERO: Aerodrome Finance is the largest decentralized exchange on Base, using a vote-escrow model in which locked AERO directs liquidity incentives.
WLD: World (formerly Worldcoin) is an identity and finance network that uses the Orb device to verify that users are unique humans. WLD is its utility and governance token.
FLOW: Flow is a layer-1 blockchain created by Dapper Labs for consumer apps, games and NFTs (such as NBA Top Shot). FLOW pays fees and secures the network.
QNT: Quant builds Overledger, interoperability software that connects multiple blockchains and enterprise systems. QNT is used to pay for licences and access to the network.
AKT: Akash Network is a decentralized cloud-computing marketplace where users lease spare server and GPU capacity. AKT secures the network and settles payments.
BEAM: Beam is a gaming-focused blockchain ecosystem governed by the Beam Foundation. BEAM is used for fees and governance across its games and infrastructure.
EGLD: MultiversX (formerly Elrond) is a sharded proof-of-stake layer-1 designed for high throughput. EGLD pays fees and secures the network through staking.
SAND: The Sandbox is a virtual world where players buy land and build, own and monetize games and experiences. SAND is used for purchases, staking and governance.
AXS: Axie Infinity is a blockchain game in which players collect and battle creatures called Axies. AXS is used for governance, staking and in-game purchases.
MANA: Decentraland is a virtual world owned by its users, where land and items are NFTs. MANA is used to buy land, wearables and other items and for governance.
ZEC: Zcash is a privacy-focused cryptocurrency that uses zero-knowledge proofs (zk-SNARKs) to allow fully shielded transactions. Like Bitcoin, it has a maximum supply of 21 million coins.
ZK: ZKsync is an Ethereum layer-2 that uses zero-knowledge proofs to scale transactions. ZK is the governance token of the ZKsync ecosystem.
ARKM: Arkham is an on-chain intelligence platform that labels blockchain addresses and entities, and also runs a crypto exchange. ARKM is its utility token.
MOG: Mog Coin is an internet-culture memecoin on Ethereum. It has no utility beyond trading and community.
IOTX: IoTeX is a layer-1 blockchain for decentralized physical infrastructure (DePIN) that connects real-world devices and their data to Web3 applications.
LPT: Livepeer is a decentralized network for video transcoding and AI video processing. LPT is staked by orchestrators who perform the work.
DYDX: dYdX is a decentralized perpetual-futures exchange running on its own Cosmos-based chain. DYDX is used for staking, governance and fee sharing.
CRV: Curve is a decentralized exchange optimized for low-slippage swaps between similar assets such as stablecoins. Vote-locked CRV directs liquidity rewards and earns fees.
SNX: Synthetix is a DeFi protocol for on-chain derivatives liquidity. SNX is staked as collateral and used for governance.
MEW: cat in a dogs world (MEW) is a cat-themed memecoin on Solana, with no utility beyond trading and community.
AIOZ: AIOZ Network is a DePIN for decentralized video streaming, storage and AI compute, where node operators earn AIOZ.
SUPER: SuperVerse (formerly SuperFarm) is a gaming and NFT ecosystem. SUPER is used for governance, staking and in-ecosystem purchases.
DASH: Dash is a digital-cash cryptocurrency forked from Bitcoin in 2014, using masternodes for instant transactions, optional privacy mixing and treasury governance.
GLM: Golem is a decentralized marketplace for computing power on Ethereum, where providers rent out spare CPU and GPU capacity for GLM.
ROSE: Oasis is a privacy-focused layer-1 blockchain whose Sapphire runtime supports confidential smart contracts. ROSE pays fees and secures the network.
METIS: Metis is an Ethereum layer-2 network with a decentralized sequencer. METIS pays gas and is used for sequencer staking.
MANTA: Manta Network builds a modular Ethereum layer-2 (Manta Pacific) focused on zero-knowledge applications. MANTA is used for fees, staking and governance.
TURBO: Turbo is an Ethereum memecoin that was reportedly designed with the help of an AI chatbot, giving it an AI theme. It has no utility beyond trading.
BOME: BOOK OF MEME is a Solana memecoin that grew out of a project to archive memes on decentralized storage.
COMP: Compound is one of the earliest decentralized lending protocols on Ethereum. COMP is used to govern the protocol.
1INCH: 1inch is a DEX aggregator that routes trades across many decentralized exchanges to find better prices. 1INCH is used for governance and staking.
ANKR: Ankr provides Web3 infrastructure, including RPC node services and liquid-staking products. ANKR is used to pay for services and to stake with node providers.
SC: Siacoin is the native coin of Sia, a decentralized storage network where hosts rent out disk space and are paid in SC under smart contracts.
FLUX: Flux is a decentralized cloud infrastructure network powered by proof-of-work, on which node operators host applications for FLUX.
PHA: Phala Network provides confidential computing for AI agents and smart contracts using trusted execution environments (TEEs). PHA pays for compute and secures the network.
NMR: Numeraire is the token of Numerai, a hedge fund that crowdsources stock-market prediction models from data scientists, who stake NMR on their models.
ZEN: Horizen is a project focused on privacy-preserving and zero-knowledge applications. ZEN is used for fees, staking and governance in its ecosystem.
LRC: Loopring is a zero-knowledge rollup protocol for trading and payments on Ethereum. LRC is used for protocol fees and incentives.
HYPE: Hyperliquid is a layer-1 blockchain built around a fully on-chain perpetual-futures and spot order book. HYPE is used for staking, gas and fee buybacks.
S: Sonic is an EVM-compatible layer-1 blockchain and the successor to Fantom; FTM holders could upgrade to S at a 1:1 ratio. S pays fees and secures the network through staking.
ASTER: Aster is a decentralized exchange for perpetual futures and spot trading, mainly on BNB Chain. ASTER is its governance and utility token.
WLFI: World Liberty Financial is a DeFi project and issuer of the USD1 stablecoin. WLFI is its governance token.
MORPHO: Morpho is a decentralized lending network that lets anyone create isolated lending markets and curated vaults. MORPHO is used for governance.
CAKE: PancakeSwap is the largest decentralized exchange on BNB Chain and also runs on several other networks. CAKE is used for liquidity incentives, governance and fee burns.
PAXG: PAX Gold is a tokenized-gold asset issued by Paxos. Each PAXG is backed by one fine troy ounce of gold held in professional vaults and is redeemable for that gold.
